records.claim: The target asteroid, Dimorphos, is a 525 feet (160 m) wide moonlet of the asteroid Didymos.
records.passage: The target asteroid, Dimorphos, is a 525 feet (160 m) wide moonlet of the asteroid Didymos; neither asteroid poses an impact threat to Earth, but their joint characteristics made them an ideal target.

records.claim: The DART spacecraft collided with Dimorphos at 14,000 mph (23,000 km/h) on 26 September 2022.
records.passage: Launched on 24 November 2021, the DART spacecraft collided with Dimorphos at 14,000 mph (23,000 km/h) on 26 September 2022 about 6.8 million miles (10.9 million kilometers) from Earth.

records.claim: The collision shortened Dimorphos's orbit around Didymos by 32 minutes, greatly in excess of the pre-defined success threshold of 73 seconds.
records.passage: The collision shortened Dimorphos's orbit around Didymos by 32 minutes, greatly in excess of the pre-defined success threshold of 73 seconds.

records.claim: The spacecraft cost US$330 million by the time it collided with Dimorphos in 2022.

narration.text: Why one crash moved an asteroid by 32 minutes.
NASA's DART hit Dimorphos on purpose in 2022.
The target was a 160-metre moonlet of Didymos.
DART struck at about 23,000 kilometres per hour.
Success needed a change of just 73 seconds.
A real threat would need years of warning to nudge in time.
So planetary defence works, if we see the asteroid early.
